qualification.reason: The document is a Request for Proposals issued by AmeriCorps NCCC for organizations to apply for teams, including application instructions, project focus areas, and partner responsibilities.

quotes.quote: We will notify applicants of award approximately six weeks prior to the project start date.

findings.title: Eligible Applicant Organizations
findings.fact: The RFP specifies that qualifying organizations include nonprofit and faith-based organizations, government entities (federal, state, and local), public schools and universities, and Native American tribal councils.
findings.business_implication: An entity outside these categories cannot be awarded a team, so eligibility must be confirmed before investing time in an application.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify your organization's legal status and category fit; if uncertain, contact the APD.

quotes.quote:
Qualifying organizations include: 
• Nonprofit and faith-based 
organizations 
• Government entities (federal, 
state, and local) 
• Public schools and universities 
• Native American tribal councils

findings.title: Application Process via APD
findings.fact: Applications are handled by Assistant Program Directors (APDs). To apply, the applicant must determine project dates, email NCCCProjectApplications@AmeriCorps.gov, follow instructions, and submit a complete application by the due date.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must initiate contact with the APD to receive instructions and the deadline; failure to do so could result in a missed opportunity.
findings.action_recommendation: Email the provided address promptly to obtain the exact due date and any required forms or templates.

quotes.quote: Applications are handled by Assistant Program Directors (APDs). To apply: • Determine the project dates when you’d like to receive a team. • Contact us by emailing NCCCProjectApplications@AmeriCorps.gov. • Follow the instructions to submit a complete application by the due date.

findings.title: Application Due Date Not Disclosed
findings.fact: The RFP mentions a due date but does not specify the exact date or timeline.
findings.business_implication: Without a known deadline, the bidder cannot schedule preparation and risks submitting late or missing the application window.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek the due date from the APD via the provided email as part of initial contact.

quotes.quote: Follow the instructions to submit a complete application by the due date.

findings.title: Partner Housing Obligations
findings.fact: The partner organization must provide housing for the team that includes a full kitchen, full bathroom with showers, cleaning supplies, and toilet paper for the duration of the project. Additionally, partners must extend lodging for the team from April 19-22, 2027, for virtual training.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must have suitable housing with specific amenities and ensure availability on the training dates, which may be outside the regular project period.
findings.action_recommendation: Inspect housing facilities to ensure they meet these specifications and reserve capacity for April 19-22, 2027.

quotes.quote: Housing for the team, to include a full kitchen, full bathroom with showers, cleaning supplies, and toilet paper for the duration of the project
Partners to extend lodging for teams Apr 19-22, 2027, so AmeriCorps NCCC staff can deliver virtual training.

findings.title: Partner Service and Supervision Requirements
findings.fact: The partner must provide at least 40 hours per week of enriching service, a broad range of service experiences, daily technical supervision, orientation to the organization and community, all project materials/tools/protective gear, any work permits, and service-learning education.
findings.business_implication: This creates a heavy operational lift: the partner must devise meaningful work, supply equipment, and supervise the team daily, which requires dedicated staff and resources.
findings.action_recommendation: Draft a project work plan, identify a technical supervisor, and budget for materials and permits.

quotes.quote:
At least 40 hours per week of enriching service that meets the needs named in your application 
• A broad range of different types of service experiences for the team 
• Daily technical supervision for the team, including on-the-job training 
• Orientation to the organization and community 
• All project materials, tools, and protective gear 
• Any work permits required to complete service 
• Service-learning education on community needs and deeper issues related to the project

findings.title: Federal Tort Claims Act Coverage
findings.fact: AmeriCorps NCCC provides coverage for the team through the Federal Tort Claims Act and Federal Employees’ Compensation Act.
findings.business_implication: The team members are covered by federal tort and compensation statutes, which may protect the partner from certain liability claims brought by team members or third parties.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the scope of FTCA coverage and clarify with program staff what responsibilities the partner retains for safety and incident reporting.

quotes.quote: Coverage for the team through the Federal Tort Claims Act and Federal Employees’ Compensation Act

findings.title: Award Notification and Training Lodging
findings.fact: Applicants will be notified of award approximately six weeks prior to the project start date. Also, partners must extend lodging for teams Apr 19-22, 2027, so AmeriCorps NCCC staff can deliver virtual training.
findings.business_implication: The bidder needs to plan for an award decision notification about six weeks before the desired project start, and must have lodging available for the training dates regardless of the project timeline.
findings.action_recommendation: Confirm the project start date and make arrangements to accommodate the April 19-22 training period.

quotes.quote: We will notify applicants of award approximately six weeks prior to the project start date.
Partners to extend lodging for teams Apr 19-22, 2027, so AmeriCorps NCCC staff can deliver virtual training.

findings.title: Ambiguity Between Project Dates and Training Lodging Extension
findings.fact: The RFP states that project dates are subject to change and include travel time, and also requires partners to extend lodging for April 19-22, 2027, but it does not clarify whether these training dates fall within the project period or are an extension beyond it.
findings.business_implication: This ambiguity could cause confusion in planning housing, staffing, and project schedule, and may affect cost calculations.
findings.action_recommendation: Ask the APD to clarify whether the April 19-22 dates are included in the project duration and how lodging extension is defined.

quotes.quote: Project dates are subject to change and INCLUDE a team’s travel time to and from the project.
Partners to extend lodging for teams Apr 19-22, 2027, so AmeriCorps NCCC staff can deliver virtual training.

findings.title: Application Stand-Out Elements
findings.fact: The RFP instructs applicants to highlight in their application any involvement of social media posts tagging @AmeriCorpsNCCC, high community exposure, service to veterans or military families, disaster prevention/preparedness/recovery/mitigation, and recruitment or coordination of other volunteers.
findings.business_implication: These elements may be used to evaluate and rank applications, giving an advantage to projects that feature them.
findings.action_recommendation: Incorporate these elements into the project design and explicitly describe them in the application.

quotes.quote: If your proposed project involves any of the following elements, please highlight them in your application: • Social media posts specifically tagging @AmeriCorpsNCCC, featuring the team’s contribution to your project and the benefit to your community • High community exposure for the team (e.g., media opportunities, interaction with public officials, large events) • Service recipients who are veterans or military families • Disaster prevention, preparedness, recovery, or mitigation • Recruitment or coordination of other volunteers in the community
